title: Quantum Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermion-Phonon Models in Circuit QED
authors: Tim Bode, Riccardo Roma, Stefan Schmitz, Alessandro Ciani, Dmitriy S. Shapiro, Dmitry Bagrets, Frank K. Wilhelm
abstract: Gate-based digital quantum simulations offer an exciting new paradigm for studying the many-body physics of strongly correlated systems. In this context, electron-phonon models are challenging for qubit-only quantum simulators, as bosonic degrees of freedom require costly finite-dimensional encodings. Here, we elaborate on an alternative approach based on a digital-analog circuit QED architecture, where fermions are encoded in transmon qubits while bosons are represented directly by microwave resonators. The central building block of this framework is a qubit-resonator Rabi gate that emulates strong electron-phonon coupling and can be implemented through a sequence of resonant Jaynes-Cummings gates interleaved with layers of single-qubit rotations. Using this Rabi gate as the fundamental unitary operation, we construct quantum circuits for the Hubbard-Holstein and Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models, which describe, respectively, strongly correlated electrons coupled to phonons and phonon-mediated interactions among Majorana fermions. We further demonstrate how nonclassical phonon physics and signatures of quantum chaos in these models can be probed through circuit simulations, and develop measurement and variational protocols tailored to near-term superconducting quantum hardware.
summary: This paper details a novel digital-analog approach to simulate complex fermion-phonon systems, like the Hubbard-Holstein model, using Circuit QED. By encoding fermions in qubits and bosons directly in resonators, they construct a fundamental Rabi gate that emulates strong electron-phonon coupling. This allows for probing exotic physics regimes relevant to correlated materials on superconducting quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary goal is the quantum simulation of strongly correlated fermion-phonon models, such as the Hubbard-Holstein and Yukawa-SYK models.
main_result: The authors successfully construct quantum circuits for these complex models using a digital-analog circuit QED architecture, demonstrating how to probe nonclassical phonon physics and chaos signatures.
method: They employ a hybrid digital-analog approach where fermions are on transmon qubits and bosons are mapped directly onto microwave resonators. The core technique involves realizing the electron-phonon coupling via a tailored qubit-resonator Rabi gate.
model_or_system: The system models include electron-phonon interactions (Hubbard-Holstein) and phonon-mediated interactions among Majorana fermions (Yukawa-SYK). The physical platform is Circuit QED, utilizing transmon qubits coupled to microwave resonators.
key_observables: Nonclassical phonon physics signatures, quantum chaos indicators (spectral statistics), and ground state properties via variational ansatz.
important_parameters: The simulation relies on controlling gate parameters like displacement amplitudes ($\varphi$) and interaction phases ($	heta$), as well as operating in both dispersive and resonant regimes of the circuit QED setup.
main_assumptions: The approach circumvents costly finite-dimensional encoding for bosons by using the resonator's physical Hilbert space. The Rabi gate implementation relies on Trotter decomposition approximations (first or second order).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pulse sequence implementing the fundamental Rabi gate protocol and show the electric circuit diagram of the coupled transmon-resonator system.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for simulating fermion-phonon models. It then details the construction of the essential qubit-resonator Rabi gate using Trotter decomposition, showing its equivalence to known gates. Finally, it applies this fundamental gate structure to build circuits for specific complex Hamiltonians like HH and Yukawa-SYK.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges advanced quantum simulation techniques (Circuit QED) with challenging condensed matter physics problems (electron-phonon coupling), providing a concrete roadmap for near-term hardware implementation of strongly correlated models.
